findings.title: Early-exit break breaks the A7 seam-isolation contract enforced by an existing test
findings.description: Option A places the cap test in the kernel body (`if k_found >= k_max and max_neighbors > 0: break`) *before* the seam call. Slice 145's A7 criterion requires the neighbor-selection logic to live only in `get_neighbors_first_k`, and `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_kernels.py::test_get_neighbors_first_k_is_only_inclusion_function` asserts that "k_found < k_max" appears at most once in the module (inside the seam). The proposed break is a second, kernel-level expression of the same cap decision. The slice asserts "A1: All slice 145 parity tests pass" while simultaneously breaking that test, and never mentions updating or re-scoping it. The design must state how the cap predicate stays single-sourced (e.g. move the whole cap decision into the seam and give the seam an explicit "should stop scanning" signal) and how the isolation test is reconciled — otherwise A1 is unsatisfiable as written.

findings.title: Gate workload for A2/A3 is not the workload that produced the baseline or the occupancy data
findings.description: The design states the operating point is "N=50k" and names `mid-flock-50k` as the default gate config, but `bench/workloads/mid-flock-50k.yaml` declares `n: 100000` with `world_size: [1536, 1536]`. The ~38 TPS baseline and the p99≈5137 cell occupancy that motivate this slice were both measured at a *different* setup: slice 148's measurement script used an inline N=50,000 workload with a 756×756 world and `cluster_radius=80` (`scripts/148_measure_cell_occupancy.py`, `148-notes.envelope-measurement.md` §2B). The A2 gate ("force_total ≥ 5× faster than slice 145 CUDA baseline") and A3 gate ("≥100 TPS") therefore compare a candidate measurement against a baseline/occupancy figure taken under a different agent count and world geometry, which makes the ratio not a like-for-like comparison and makes the expected candidate counts (~555 agents/cell at S=3) unreliable for the named gate config. The design should name the exact workload (and N) used for both the baseline capture and the gate run.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough uses a nonexistent script and unsupported CLI flags
findings.description: Every command in the walkthrough invokes `python scripts/bench.py --backend quadrants-fused --config mid-flock-50k --subdivision-factor 1 --ticks 200` (and `--N`, `--parity-check`). There is no `scripts/bench.py` (only `scripts/148_*.py`), and the actual CLI (`src/migratory/bench/cli.py`) exposes only `--workload <name>`, `--backend`, `--workload-dir`, `--results-dir` — no `--config`, `--N`, `--ticks`, `--subdivision-factor`, or `--parity-check`. The harness also drives tick counts from the workload YAML (`warmup_ticks`/`measure_ticks`), not from a CLI flag. The walkthrough therefore cannot be executed as written, and the new `subdivision_factor` input has no defined plumbing (the task file proposes it as a `Workload` YAML field, which is a different mechanism than the CLI flag the design assumes).

findings.title: Config plumbing names a `BenchConfig` type that does not exist, and omits the kernel call sites
findings.description: The Component Interactions diagram starts from a `BenchConfig` object supplying `cell_size` and `subdivision_factor S`; no such type exists in the codebase — the harness configuration is the YAML-backed `Workload` dataclass (`src/migratory/bench/workload.py`) and `GpuAgentState` derives `cell_size = max_query_radius * DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER` at setup (`src/migratory/bench/backends/quadrants_fused_state.py:150`). The design also does not name the integration points for the new kernel parameter: `fused_force_integrate_kernel` is called from two places (`quadrants_fused_backend.py::tick_once` and `quadrants_fused_kernels.py::run_fused_tick`), and `GpuAgentState.setup`/`DEFAULT_CELL_SIZE_MULTIPLIER` must change for `cell_size` to become `query_radius / S`. Without these, the "same setup()/tick() interface, only cell_size and S change" claim is not verifiable.

findings.title: Cell subdivision changes the accepted neighbor set in a way the parity criterion does not cover
findings.description: The design asserts "The scan covers the same physical radius — correct neighborhood is preserved." That holds only for the radius bound; the *set* of visited candidates changes with `cell_size` (a (2S+1)×(2S+1) walk over smaller cells reaches a different set of agents than a 3×3 walk over larger cells, including agents in corner cells that a coarse walk never visited), and combined with first-k-found the accepted set is order-dependent and therefore different. Since first-k-found already has a documented parity gap vs. the CPU's k-nearest, this compounds it. A4 (statistical parity within 20% of numpy) is asserted as the check, but the design does not state the expected effect or a per-configuration acceptance rule for S=3 versus S=1 — in particular, S=3 changes the *population* of first-k-found picks in a way that can shift mean speed/mean NN distance by more than the 20% band independent of any bug. The design should say how S=1 vs S=3 parity is compared and what happens if it falls outside the band.

findings.title: Early exit is unconditional but the divergence cost is asserted, not bounded, at the low-density operating point
findings.description: The divergence analysis justifies the break only at the dense operating point ("at the operating point where this matters (dense flock, N=50k)") and notes that "divergence overhead is proportional to the *spread* of exit iterations within a warp — small at high density, larger at low density." No fallback or guard is defined for the low-density case where agents hit the cap at very different iteration counts (the `uniform` formation measured p99=184 agents/cell in slice 148's notes, where the counter-gating cost was already low). The `max_neighbors > 0` guard covers the uncapped path but not the "capped yet low-density" path, where the break could plausibly be a net regression. The design should state the expected behavior/measurement for the low-density (uniform) formation and what result would trigger reverting to counter-gating.

findings.title: Register-spill criterion (A5) is not measurable with the tooling the design names
findings.description: A5 requires "local memory per thread = 0 (confirmed via `nvcc --ptxas-info` or benchmark log)" and Step 4 says to "Look for `lmem` in the bench log output (Quadrants/Taichi emits ptxas info when `TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS=1` or equivalent)". On the actual CUDA host, slice 148 established that `ptxas`, `cuobjdump`, and `nvcc` are **not installed** (`148-notes.envelope-measurement.md` §2A), and the working method was PTX inspection of the Quadrants kernel cache for `.local` declarations (`.local` = 0 in the baseline). The `TI_PRINT_KERNEL_STATS`/`lmem` route is therefore likely unavailable on the gate host, leaving A5 unverifiable as specified. The design should name the PTX-cache inspection method that slice 148 actually used.

findings.title: Slice 149 correctly preserves the fused-tick architectural boundary and slice 146's integration contract
findings.description: The "No changes to" list (TickResult/world-server interface, parity infrastructure, numpy/numba backends, agent state field layout) matches architecture 140's "same pattern, different backend — except the GPU fused tick" principle, and the explicit statement that the `quadrants-fused` external API is unchanged keeps slice 146 unblocked as the plan requires. The Out of Scope list correctly defers distance-ranked k-nearest, GPU prefix sum, and Metal-specific tuning — all of which the plan assigns to later slices.
